correctness.rationale: The exact setting is C=[-1,1]^2 and z_c=(c,c), 0<=c<1, with positively oriented nondegenerate boundary triangle and cyclic gauge lengths. Translation gives K_c=[-b,a]^2, a=1-c>0,b=1+c and p_c(x,y)=max(x/a,-x/b,y/a,-y/b). For common side lambda>0, q_i=(P_{i+1}-P_i)/lambda lie on the gauge boundary and sum to zero. Choose one active supporting coordinate on each q_i; with 3 choices and only 2 coordinate axes, at least two share an axis. Active values (a,-b) force lambda b<=2 by the square coordinate diameter; (a,a) imply third coordinate -2a in [-b,a], feasible only b>=2a (c>=1/3), and force 2a lambda<=2; (-b,-b) demand 2b<=a, impossible since b>=a>0. Thus lambda<=2/b if c<1/3 and lambda<=max(2/b,1/a) otherwise. For c<=1/3, t=-b+2a/b, the three vertices (a,t),(-b,t),(t,-b) lie on the boundary, have strictly positive determinant and cyclic gauge length 2/b. For c>=1/3, (-b,-c),(-c,-b),(a,-b) have consecutive side vectors (1,-1),(1,0),(-2,1), positive signed area, and all gauge lengths 1/a because b>=2a. At c=1/3 branches meet at 3/2. First branch strictly decreases, second strictly increases; reflection interchanges the orientations and diagonal square isometries generate all equivalent minimizing origins. End c=1 excluded because the origin is on the boundary and the gauge degenerates. Independent exact rational checks at eight c samples confirm the witnesses; the continuum conclusion follows from the case proof rather than the samples.
residual_risks: No numerical search is used to prove the continuum result; samples test only explicit branches.
Not an all-origin or all-polygon classification; claims require oriented cyclic lengths and 0<=c<1.

originality.rationale: The 2004 primary paper explicitly fixes one square origin at diagonal distance ratio 1:2 and proves the 3/2 ceiling there; its other theorem gives a 1.25 existence guarantee for arbitrary Minkowski disks. The 2009 article abstract states universal 3/2 existence/sharpness for arbitrary disks, which does not determine the maximal inscribed equilateral side length for each translated-square origin. The 2025 open full-text review concerns symmetric normed planes and explicitly cites the 2004/2009 papers as the asymmetric exception. Independent semantic searches under diagonal/off-center-gauge aliases and direct formula searches found the assigned Resultary self-copy but no independent formula or stronger implication. The full two-branch function for all 0<=c<1 and its unique minimizing orbit are best-of-knowledge original, qualified by 2003/2009 full-text access limitations and possible unindexed notes.
residual_risks: 2003 Fabińska–Lassak same-authors paper was not available in primary full text; institutional retrieval returned a worker error; this alone is not scientific failure.
The final 2009 journal article full text was not independently secured; only its abstract was verified and a mismatched author-posted working text was inspected.
Potential historical equivalence under asymmetric gauge/oriented chord terminology in unindexed work remains possible; lack of search hits is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The family is a canonical one-parameter deformation of the 2004 square sharpness witness: fix the square and displace only its Minkowski origin along the same diagonal. The exact maximum side-length function changes its active support mechanism at c=1/3; the unique minimizer and sharp 3/2 threshold explain structurally why the historical 1:2 diagonal ratio is optimal within this geometric family. This is a complete continuous classification of a natural invariant and object, not an arbitrary finite computation or simple restatement of the special witness. It may be used in studying stability, extremizers, and perturbations of asymmetric Minkowski triangle constants. It is a modest specific geometric result, not a theorem for arbitrary disks or off-diagonal origins.
residual_risks: The case distinction is elementary once the translated-square gauge is chosen; the mathematical contribution is the full natural parameter law and extremal orbit rather than a broad new method.
Does not optimize over all interior origin positions, which could have additional branches.
